source_user: Calculation case 285: a model has 56 layers, 2 KV heads, head dimension 128, sequence length 3072, and BF16/FP16 KV values. Estimate bytes for one request's K/V cache. Show the formula and report GiB.
source_assistant: Use 2 × layers × sequence_length × KV_heads × head_dim × bytes_per_value. Here this is 2 × 56 × 3072 × 2 × 128 × 2 = 176160768 bytes = 0.164062 GiB. This excludes allocator metadata and other runtime memory.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions that must be checked against config.json and the serving engine before this number drives a capacity decision: (1) standard attention with exactly one K tensor and one V tensor per layer — this is the source of the leading factor of 2; (2) the head count used is num_key_value_heads (GQA/MQA), not num_attention_heads; (3) no sliding-window attention, no cross-attention KV, and no MLA-style latent KV compression — each of these breaks the linear-in-sequence-length model, sliding-window by capping the effective S at the window, MLA by storing a compressed latent instead of full K/V; (4) sequence length means total context (prompt + generated tokens), not prompt alone.

Formula: kv_bytes = 2 (K and V) x num_layers x seq_len x num_kv_heads x head_dim x bytes_per_value.

Substituting: 2 x 56 x 3072 x 2 x 128 x 2 = 176160768 bytes = 168.0000 MiB = 0.164062 GiB (GiB = bytes / 2^30). Dtype assumed: BF16/FP16 (2 bytes/value).

Case-specific notes:
- num_kv_heads = 2 is a hard tensor-parallel constraint: TP must divide 2 for KV to shard cleanly (TP in {1,2}). At higher TP the engine either replicates KV per rank — so aggregate KV grows linearly with TP while per-GPU KV stops shrinking — or refuses the config outright.
- This case is depth-dominated (56 layers): the layer-linear term means KV dtype quantization at best halves the total, while cutting max context or per-request concurrency is the only lever that changes the shape of the curve.

Boundary conditions the raw figure does not capture, each pushing real allocation upward:
- PagedAttention block rounding: allocation is ceil(seq_len/B_blk) x B_blk tokens for block size B_blk, so short or ragged requests waste up to (B_blk - 1) tokens of KV each.
- Prefix caching / radix-tree reuse keeps blocks resident after a request completes, so steady-state KV exceeds concurrency x per-request KV.
- Speculative decoding and beam search hold KV for draft or branch tokens that are later discarded.
- Engines pre-reserve a KV pool at startup (e.g. gpu_memory_utilization in vLLM), so nvidia-smi reports the pool, not live occupancy; per-request arithmetic tells you how many requests fit in the pool, not how much memory the process uses.
- Disaggregated prefill/decode and KV offload paths (Mooncake-style pooled KV store, NVIDIA Dynamo KV-aware routing) move this same byte count across the network or into host/NVMe tiers; the interconnect then bounds it — at these sizes a 200 Gb/s RoCE link moves the cache in roughly 7.05 ms at line rate, which is the floor for any migration or cache-transfer decision, before RDMA registration and congestion-control effects.

Falsifiable test: run the engine with max_num_seqs=1 and a single request padded to exactly this context length, then compare the engine's reported GPU KV cache size (vLLM logs it in tokens; multiply by per-token KV bytes = 57344 B/token here) against this derivation. Deviation beyond about 10% falsifies one of the four assumptions above — most often the GQA head count or an undeclared quantized-KV scale overhead.

Rollback gate: if after raising concurrency on this sizing the engine reports any preemption/swap rate above 1%, p99 TTFT regresses more than 20% versus the pre-change baseline, or any OOM appears in engine logs, revert to the previous max_num_seqs / max_model_len and re-derive with measured per-token KV bytes instead of the analytic value.

Silent on sliding-window attention and MLA latent KV, where the linear-in-sequence-length model is simply wrong.
